nodes.summary: For all sufficiently large $k$, (Maynard (2015), Proposition 4.3(3)). In particular $M_k \to \infty$, which, with the Bombieri–Vinogradov level, gives any number of primes in infinitely many translates of a long enough admissible tuple; this is the source of Maynard's explicit bound for gaps between $m + 1$ primes.
nodes.title: Growth of $M_k$

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb N$, the indicator of the box $[0, \tfrac{1}{k+1}]^k$ is an admissible profile: it is bounded and measurable, it vanishes outside Maynard's simplex because $k \cdot \tfrac{1}{k+1} \le 1$, and $I_k$ and every $J_k^{(m)}$ are positive on it. Hence the set of ratios whose supremum is $M_k$ is nonempty, including for $k = 0$, where the cube $[0,1]^0$ is a point.
nodes.title: Admissible profiles exist

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a finite set of natural numbers, $w : \mathbb N \to \mathbb R$ with $w_n \ge 0$ for $n \in s$, $H$ a finite set of shifts and $\rho \in \mathbb R$. If then some $n \in s$ has more than $\rho$ of the numbers $n + h$, $h \in H$, prime, that is at least $\lfloor \rho + 1 \rfloor$ of them.
nodes.title: GPY detection principle, finite form

nodes.summary: Maynard's variational quantity for $k = 105$ satisfies $M_{105} > 4$ (Maynard (2015), Proposition 4.3(2)). With the Bombieri–Vinogradov level $\theta = \tfrac12 - \varepsilon$ this gives $\theta M_{105}/2 > 1$, so every admissible $105$-tuple has infinitely many translates with two primes; with an admissible $105$-tuple of diameter $600$ this is $\liminf_n (p_{n+1} - p_n) \le 600$ (Theorem 1.3). nodes.summary: Let $p_0 = 2 < p_1 = 3 < \cdots$ be the primes, indexed from $0$. Let $H$ be a finite set of natural numbers with $b \le a + D$ for all $a, b \in H$. If infinitely many $n$ have more than $m$ of the $n + h$, $h \in H$, prime, then that is $\liminf_j (p_{j+m} - p_j) \le D$. Suppose that for every $\delta \in (0, \delta_0)$ there are weights $w_N(n) \ge 0$ and a normalisation $B(N)$, positive for large $N$, with where $S_1, S_2$ are the sums of the limiting step. Then infinitely many $n$ have more than $\rho$ of the $n + h$, $h \in H$, prime.
nodes.title: Maynard's reduction for one weight profile

nodes.summary: Let $w_N(n) \ge 0$ and set If $B(N) > 0$ for all large $N$, $S_1(N)/B(N) \to I$, $S_2(N)/B(N) \to J$ and $\rho I < J$, then infinitely many $n$ have more than $\rho$ of the $n + h$ prime.
nodes.title: From the asymptotics of $S_1$ and $S_2$ to infinitely many prime-rich translates

nodes.summary: A function $F : \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ is an admissible profile if it is measurable and bounded, vanishes outside Maynard's simplex $\mathcal R_k$, and satisfies $I_k(F) \ne 0$ and $J_k^{(m)}(F) \ne 0$ for every $m$.
nodes.title: Admissible profiles for $M_k$

nodes.summary: For an admissible profile $F$, $I_k(F) > 0$: the integral of $F^2$ is non-negative, and it is non-zero by assumption.
nodes.title: $I_k$ of an admissible profile is positive

nodes.summary: For $F : \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$, (Maynard (2015), Proposition 4.1), the normalised main term of the sum $S_1$. The Lean definition is the Lebesgue integral over the cube $[0, 1]^k$; for a non-square-integrable $F$ it takes Mathlib's junk value $0$.
nodes.title: Maynard's functional $I_k$

nodes.summary: For $F : \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ and $1 \le m \le k$, (Maynard (2015), Proposition 4.1), the normalised contribution of the shift $h_m$ to the sum $S_2$. The Lean definition integrates over the whole cube $[0, 1]^k$ a function that does not depend on the $m$-th coordinate, which gives the same value since that coordinate ranges over an interval of length $1$.
nodes.title: Maynard's functional $J_k^{(m)}$

nodes.summary: the supremum over admissible profiles (Maynard (2015), Proposition 4.2). If the primes have level of distribution $\theta$, then every admissible $k$-tuple has infinitely many translates containing at least $\lceil \theta M_k / 2 \rceil$ primes; see the reduction.
nodes.title: Maynard's variational quantity $M_k$

nodes.summary: For $F : \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$, the ratio whose supremum over admissible profiles is $M_k$ (Maynard (2015), Proposition 4.2), built from $I_k$ and $J_k^{(m)}$.
nodes.title: Maynard's ratio

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb N$, the set on which Maynard's profiles $F$ are supported (Maynard (2015), Proposition 4.1). The constraint $\sum_i x_i \le 1$ reflects the support condition $\prod_i d_i < R$ on the sieve weights $\lambda_{d_1, \dots, d_k}$.
nodes.title: Maynard's simplex

nodes.summary: For a finite set $H$ of natural numbers and $n \in \mathbb N$, the number of prime translates is the inner sum in the Goldston–Pintz–Yıldırım detecting sum $S(N, \rho)$ of Maynard (2015), display (2.1). Shifts are natural numbers, as in Maynard's and GPY's definition of a $k$-tuple $\{h_1, \dots, h_k\}$ of distinct non-negative integers.
nodes.title: Number of prime translates

nodes.summary: Maynard's variational quantity for $k = 5$ satisfies $M_5 > 2$ (Maynard (2015), Proposition 4.3(1)). With the admissible $5$-tuple $\{0, 2, 6, 8, 12\}$ and the Elliott–Halberstam level $\theta = 1 - \varepsilon$, the reduction gives two primes in infinitely many translates, hence $\liminf_n (p_{n+1} - p_n) \le 12$ under Elliott–Halberstam (Maynard (2015), proof of Theorem 1.4).
nodes.title: $M_5 > 2$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
